newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Selectors meet to choose Hong Kong's leader.
newsitem.headline: Selectors meet to choose Hong Kong's leader.

text.p: China inaugurated a carefully chosen electoral college on Friday responsible for choosing the man who will lead Hong Kong when the British colony reverts to China next year.
Pro-democracy demonstrators staging noisy protests scuffled with police when China's Foreign Minister Qian Qichen arrived to open the meeting in Hong Kong.
"The responsibility you shoulder is onerous," Qian told the assembled panel in his opening adress.

The 400 members of the Selection Committee, all of them Hong Kong citizens, are charged with choosing Hong Kong's post-colonial Chief Executive and a 60-member controversial provisional legislature over the next month.

Qian called the panel representative of all sections of Hong Kong society and slammed Britain which had appointed all 28 of its colonial governors from London without referring to the wishes of Hong Kong people.
He called the Selection Committee the beginning of genuine democracy in Hong Kong.
More than a century and a half of colonial rule ends at midnight on June 30 next year when Britain hands the colony and its six million people over to China.
Qian said Beijing had not preordained a candidate.
Two businessmen and two former senior judges are regarded as the front-runners for the post of Chief Executive.
